title: Rubber Duck Debugging and The Pragmatic Programmer (1999)
explainer: The practice of explaining a problem out loud before asking someone else for help traces to a story in Andrew Hunt and David Thomas's 1999 book The Pragmatic Programmer, about a programmer who carried a rubber duck and explained his code to it, line by line, whenever he got stuck. It captures something real about getting unstuck on your own: the act of articulating a problem precisely, to anyone or anything, often surfaces the misunderstanding before you even finish the sentence.

title: Information Foraging Theory (1999)
explainer: In the 1990s, PARC researchers Peter Pirolli and Stuart Card noticed that people searching for information online behave like animals foraging for food - following scent-like cues toward a promising source and abandoning it once the payoff drops too low, a theory they formalized in a 1999 paper. It explains why skimming a table of contents or a changelog for the right-looking heading, rather than reading a doc page linearly top to bottom, is an efficient strategy for getting unstuck rather than a shortcut around "real" reading.
